node.title: Re^3: Idiomatic Perl?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Is it okay to just do my $str = chomp();?

No, because [doc://chomp] is a bit special: it modifies its argument(s) and returns the total number of characters removed from all its arguments. The code you showed would fail because chomp wants to modify its arguments, but can't modify itself.

The reason chomp( my $str = ); works is because a scalar assignment in Perl like ( my $str = ) is modifiable (an "lvalue"), as described in [doc://perlop#Assignment-Operators]: "Modifying an assignment is equivalent to doing the assignment and then modifying the variable that was assigned to."

If you want to be a little bit more verbose, what you can do is:

my $str = ; chomp($str);
